analysis.title: European Morning Note
key_insights: UBS sales and trading commentary (not UBS Research) from 28-Oct-2026: VGZ6 (Euro Stoxx 50 futures) is -0.1% in early trading.
US markets traded sideways after the European close, with the S&P up 60bps and the Nasdaq up 1.2%. Brent crude fell 1.6% to $114 a barrel.

Iran's Mojtaba Khamenei called for pursuing the conditions set out by his country's officials with the aim of ending the war, in a meeting with Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaee, per a Telegram statement.
US consumer confidence unexpectedly rose in October for the first time in four months, on brighter views of the job market and business conditions.
GOOG and MSFT results after the close today are described as pivotal.

UBS base case for this evening's FOMC is rates held unchanged, likely by a 10-2 vote, with Warsh keeping a hawkish message that there is 'more work to do' on inflation. The pause reflects the proximity of the mid-term elections and sticky inflation around 3%, rather than accelerating inflation or an overheating economy, which reduces the urgency to hike immediately.

Asian stocks had their biggest gain in a week. The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose as much as 1.5%, led by Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. The Kospi gained 7%, its most in nearly three months. HSI was +0.4% and CSI300 +0.2%.
The UBS London sales desk saw a pause in recent elevated flows yesterday. In a quiet session it saw buyers of EM (MEs) after Monday's selling, and buyers of FTSE and OMX in Europe.
Calendar today: 12:30 UK Budget and 12:30 US Wholesale Inventories MoM for September (0.5% expected).
earnings_insights: GOOG and MSFT report results after the close on 10/28, flagged by UBS as pivotal. No estimates are given.
